# omaddons for agents

omaddons manages World of Warcraft addons for every client on this Linux machine, with one binary of 59 commands. Every addon change is a journaled transaction that `omaddons undo` reverts, a preview can be applied exactly as it was shown, and with `--json` every command prints one envelope whose errors name their fix, as an argv when the fix is a command. Ask the binary for the rest: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>` and `omaddons robot-docs errors`.

## The core loop

1. `omaddons status --json`: every client, what needs attention, and the next commands in `commands[]`.
2. Preview a change before you make it, unless the user asked for exactly that change: add `--dry-run --json`. A preview changes no addon or setting; when it would change something, it stores a plan and returns `data.plan_id` (else `null`).
3. Show the user `data.approval.selection` (each change) and `data.approval.reasons` (each effect beyond a routine change). When they approve, run `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`.
4. Lost an `apply`'s output? Run `omaddons plans show <plan_id> --json` before you preview or change anything again: it says whether the plan committed.
5. Something broken? See the doctor loop.
6. The escape hatch: `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts the newest run an agent made.

Pass `--actor agent` and `--reason` on every change: history records both.

## Reading the envelope

With `--json`, stdout is one JSON object: `ok`, `schema_version`, `tool_version`, `command` and `exit_code`; then `partial` and `data` on success, or `error` on failure; then `warnings`, `commands` and `meta`.

- `ok` is `exit_code == 0`. A failure's `error` carries `code`, `message`, `fix`, `fix_argv`, `alternatives`, `retryable` and `details`; `fix_argv` is `null` when the fix is prose or needs a value only you can supply. `check_failed` (exit 6, from `--check` or `--strict`) keeps `data` and `partial` too.
- `partial: true` (exit 0) means some items failed; `data` says which and why.
- `warnings` never change the exit code. `commands` are the suggested next steps, each with `action`, `command`, `argv` and `destructive`; ask the user before running one marked `destructive: true`.
- Run `fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv` and `commands[].argv` as argv arrays, never through a shell. Never parse `message`, `fix`, `command` or human output: branch on `exit_code`, `error.code` and `data`.
- Doctor commands put their report (`state`, `summary`, `findings`) at the top level, with no `data`; there findings (exit 1) are a report with no `error`.
- `schema_version` is the contract version. A `1.x` release only adds keys, enum values, codes and actions, so ignore the ones you do not know.

Each `commands[]` entry names its `action`. This table's `Destructive` is the action's worst case; an entry's own `destructive` is that instance's, so trust it over the table: an `apply` is as destructive as its plan.

| Action               | What it does                                                 | Destructive |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `undo`               | Undo one transaction                                         | yes         |
| `undo_run`           | Undo every transaction of one run                            | yes         |
| `update`             | Install the available updates                                | no          |
| `check_updates`      | Check every client for updates                               | no          |
| `adopt`              | Adopt folders installed by hand                              | no          |
| `adopt_folder`       | Adopt one folder identified only by a guess                  | no          |
| `adopt_with_ref`     | Adopt one folder from a chosen source                        | no          |
| `install`            | Install an addon                                             | no          |
| `search`             | Search the sources for an addon                              | no          |
| `info`               | Show which clients an addon's newest release likely loads on | no          |
| `reinstall`          | Reinstall an addon whose files were changed                  | no          |
| `inspect`            | Show a client's addons in detail                             | no          |
| `status`             | Run a full status, which builds the cache                    | no          |
| `remove_orphans`     | Remove dependencies nothing requires any more                | yes         |
| `list_unmanaged`     | List the folders omaddons does not manage                    | no          |
| `forget_target`      | Forget a client that is no longer on this machine            | yes         |
| `backup_create`      | Back up a client's settings                                  | no          |
| `refresh_backups`    | Refresh a client's backup summary                            | no          |
| `check_errors`       | Read a client's Lua errors                                   | no          |
| `dismiss_errors`     | Dismiss a client's current Lua errors                        | no          |
| `install_buggrabber` | Install BugGrabber so Lua errors are captured                | no          |
| `reinstall_widget`   | Bring the bar widget up to date                              | no          |
| `enable_widget`      | Put the omaddons widget on the bar                           | no          |
| `apply`              | Run exactly what a dry run stored                            | yes         |
| `doctor_explain`     | Explain one failure mode and its instances                   | no          |
| `doctor_fix`         | Run exactly the repair a doctor fix dry run showed           | no          |
| `install_skill`      | Install the omaddons skill into another agent's skill folder | no          |

## Exit codes

| Code | Name           | Meaning                                                                                                                                 | Retryable           |
| ---- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| 0    | `ok`           | Success, including partial success: per-item failures are listed in data, mirrored in warnings, and flagged partial: true               | n/a                 |
| 1    | `failed`       | Runtime failure: network, source, archive integrity, I/O, state, internal                                                               | see error.retryable |
| 2    | `usage`        | Unknown command or flag, bad argument, bad ref syntax                                                                                   | no                  |
| 3    | `not_found`    | Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous                                                                         | no                  |
| 4    | `refused`      | Safety refusal: running client, protected folder, ownership or case conflict, unsafe archive, wrong flavor, undo conflict, blocked host | no                  |
| 5    | `locked`       | Another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout                                                                         | yes                 |
| 6    | `check_failed` | An opt-in assertion failed (--check, --strict)                                                                                          | no                  |

Every `doctor` command uses its own exit dictionary:

| Code | Name                     | Meaning                                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | `healthy`                | every selected check ran to completion and found nothing                                                                            |
| 1    | `findings_present`       | the run completed and reports findings, a check that could not finish among them                                                    |
| 2    | `fix_partial`            | a fix ran and some findings remain                                                                                                  |
| 3    | `fix_failed_rolled_back` | a fix failed and was rolled back; nothing changed                                                                                   |
| 4    | `refused_unsafe`         | refused before changing anything: a safety precondition, a missing --force, a conflict, a stale preview or an over-budget selection |
| 5    | `concurrency_lost`       | another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout                                                                     |
| 6    | `online_required`        | the selection needs the network: add --online                                                                                       |
| 64   | `usage_error`            | unknown command or flag, or a bad argument                                                                                          |
| 66   | `no_input`               | a target, run, failure mode or other input was not found, or is ambiguous                                                           |
| 73   | `cannot_create`          | the run directory could not be created                                                                                              |
| 74   | `io_error`               | a runtime failure: I/O, state, network or internal                                                                                  |

## Targets and refs

`-t` names a client in any of these forms, tried in this order:

| Form            | Example                  | Selects                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`           | `<key>`                  | one client by its stable key, as `omaddons targets --json` lists it |
| `id`            | `retail`, `era`, `wotlk` | one client by its id                                                |
| `product_code`  | `wow_classic_era`        | the client of that Battle.net product                               |
| `flavor_folder` | `_retail_`               | the client in that flavor folder                                    |
| `game_mode`     | `sod`                    | the client that runs the mode (`sod` selects Classic Era)           |
| `family`        | `mainline`               | every client of the family                                          |
| `path`          | `<client dir>`           | the client at that install root, client directory or `AddOns` path  |
| `all`           | `all`                    | every client                                                        |

The client always goes in `-t`, as in `omaddons update -t retail`. A command that acts on one client, such as `install` or `remove`, answers `target_ambiguous` when `-t` matches several, with one candidate per `fix_argv` and `alternatives` entry. `-t all` selects every client, test clients included. `omaddons targets --json` lists the clients.

Refs: a catalog name, `gh:Owner/Repo` or `Owner/Repo`, `wowi:<id>`, `tukui:<slug>`, `wowace:<slug>`, `git:https://…#<rev>`, `url:https://…`, a pasted GitHub, WoWInterface, Tukui or WowAce link, or a local zip or folder. `omaddons search <words> --json` finds one.

## The safety model

- **Transactions.** Each change to a client is one journaled transaction, and a crash leaves each client wholly old or wholly new. Bare `omaddons undo` reverts the newest run, `--last-by agent` the newest run by an agent, `undo <tx>` one transaction and `undo --run <run>` one run, SavedVariables included. An undo is a change too: running the same undo again puts the change back. Settings commands, `errors dismiss` and every `backup` command but `restore` are never undone.
- **Running clients.** While a modern or 3.3.5a client runs, the default policy lets an update that keeps the loaded TOC land (`data.reload_required: "reload"`: the user types `/reload`) and refuses what the game would notice, such as removing a loaded addon, with `game_running`; other private-server clients refuse every change. `--while-running` lifts those refusals; add it only when the user asks. SavedVariables are never written while the client runs, whatever the flags.
- **Previews bind.** `omaddons apply <plan_id>` runs exactly the stored preview, and `--if-match <data.precondition>` binds a typed run the same way. If anything changed since, the run refuses with `plan_stale`, never retryable here: `details.changed` names what moved, or `details.reason` says why the plan cannot apply (`expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`), and `fix_argv` previews again. A plan lives 24 hours; once it is gone from the cache, `apply` answers `plan_not_found`.
- **Per client.** On each client a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them. A run over several clients is one transaction per client and can end partial: `data.outcomes[]` gives each client's `status` (`committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`) with its `tx` or `error_code`. No run over several clients is atomic.
- **Lost output.** `plans show` changes nothing. Its `state` is `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`, and `evidence.targets` lists each client that committed, with its `tx`. A second `apply` of an applied plan refuses with `already_applied`.
- **The doctor.** `omaddons doctor` changes nothing outside its own run record. `doctor fix` keeps what it overwrites or sets aside, and deletes nothing. An undo reverts a repair only while nothing the repair touched has changed since; otherwise it refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything.
- **Two kinds of run.** History's `run` (one invocation, a ULID) is reverted with `undo --run <run>`. A doctor run (a directory named by its UTC time and a ULID) is reverted with `doctor undo <doctor_run>`, which is the fix `undo --run` gives a doctor run.

## Things omaddons will NEVER do

1. Delete your files during a change. Removals go into undo snapshots or a quarantine, and only `backup prune`, `doctor gc --before --yes` and retention delete, by their documented rules.
2. Write into `Interface/AddOns` outside a transaction, touch a `Blizzard_*` folder, or follow a symlinked folder.
3. Write SavedVariables while the client runs, or parse or edit them, except reading BugGrabber's.
4. Rewrite `history.jsonl`, `config.toml` or `addons.toml` behind your back (`config set` and `export --write` edit them only when asked).
5. Contact a host outside the allowlist, make a request under `--offline`, or send a credential anywhere but its own service.
6. Run a shell, or interpret a string as a command: argv only.
7. Prompt for input, or print ANSI under `--json`.
8. Act on state it cannot read (a newer or damaged journal, record or history line): it refuses and says why.

## Recipes

Run each recipe's commands in order; a `#` line says where a value comes from. Preview anything the user did not ask for exactly.

Update every addon on every client; one `omaddons undo` reverts it all:

```sh
omaddons update --json --actor agent --reason "the user asked to update every addon"
```

What is broken (`doctor` exits 1 on findings):

```sh
omaddons status --json
omaddons doctor --json
```

Install an addon on one client:

```sh
omaddons install weakauras -t era --json --actor agent
```

A legacy addon from git:

```sh
omaddons install git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main -t wotlk --json
```

Preview, then apply exactly what was shown:

```sh
omaddons install dbm -t retail --dry-run --json
# <plan_id> is data.plan_id of the command above
omaddons apply <plan_id> --json
```

Undo what the agent did today (an earlier run: `undo --run <run>` from the list):

```sh
omaddons history --by agent --since 1d --json
omaddons undo --last-by agent --json
```

Pending updates with their release notes:

```sh
omaddons outdated --changelog --json
```

A fresh machine, from the old one's `omaddons export`, at its versions and the very archives it recorded (another archive fails `hash_mismatch` with `details.reason: "lock_mismatch"`):

```sh
omaddons sync addons.toml --locked --json
```

## Errors you will meet

omaddons has 43 error codes and 55 warning codes. `retryable: true` means the same command may succeed if run again, as for `locked` (another omaddons is committing) or `rate_limited` after `details.reset_at`. `game_running` means the game must exit first; when its `fix_argv` adds `--while-running`, run it only if the user asks. The ones agents meet most:

- `usage` (exit 2 `usage`; retryable: no). The command line was not accepted: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or id, or a missing or relative `HOME`. Fix: the corrected command line or the closest command, else `omaddons help <command>`, or prose (a template, `HOME`, an id).
- `target_not_found` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). No client matches the selection, a required client is unavailable, or the chosen path contains no client. Fix: `omaddons targets` (`--rescan`) or the same command with `-t <id>`, or prose: `omaddons targets add <path>`.
- `target_ambiguous` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). The selection matches several clients where exactly one is required. Fix: the same command with `-t <candidate>` (`--from`/`--to` for `copy`), one alternative per other candidate.
- `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). An addon, source or backup selection has several possible matches. Fix: the same command naming one candidate exactly, one alternative per candidate, or a listing to choose from.
- `not_found` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). A requested addon, release, path, transaction, run, backup or undo snapshot was not found or cannot serve that request. Fix: a listing to choose from, `omaddons search <name>`, a corrected `omaddons install <ref>`, its help, or prose.
- `not_managed` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). The requested addon or folder is not managed by omaddons on the selected client. Fix: `omaddons list -t <id>`, `omaddons install <name>` or `omaddons adopt <folder>`, or prose for a protected or linked one.
- `no_compatible_release` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). No available release or archive candidate loads on the selected client or belongs to the requested release channel. Fix: `omaddons install <ref>` (other channel, version or `git:` ref), `omaddons targets`, or prose: pin or use a local file.
- `wrong_flavor` (exit 4 `refused`; retryable: no). The supplied archive does not load on this client, an adopted group has no loadable folder, or an imported backup belongs to another family. Fix: `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged`, the same command with `-t <id>` or `--force`, or prose: use a build for this client.
- `game_running` (exit 4 `refused`; retryable: no). The client's running state or running policy forbids the requested change. Fix: the same command with `--while-running` for a policy refusal, else prose: quit the game first.
- `unmanaged_folder` (exit 4 `refused`; retryable: no). A requested destination folder exists outside omaddons management or is a symlink that cannot be replaced. Fix: `omaddons adopt <folder> --ref <ref> -t <id>`, the same command with `--force`, `omaddons list -t <id>`, or prose.
- `undo_conflict` (exit 4 `refused`; retryable: no). The transaction was already undone, or later changes or unreadable history prevent its reversal. Fix: `omaddons undo <tx>` of the later change or with `--saved-variables restore`, or prose: move a folder, or upgrade.
- `plan_stale` (exit 1 `failed`; retryable: per instance). What a command planned or previewed no longer matches the state it would change; an instance is retryable when re-planning raised it, never under `--if-match`. Fix: the same command again after re-planning, or the same command with `--dry-run` for `--if-match`.
- `plan_not_found` (exit 3 `not_found`; retryable: no). No readable stored plan answers to the given id, or its file exceeds the size limit. Fix: `omaddons help apply`, or prose: preview the change again with its command's `--dry-run`.
- `network` (exit 1 `failed`; retryable: per instance). A request failed at the network or decoding layer, or a git subprocess timed out or failed outside download; an instance is retryable except after too many redirects or an undecodable encoding. Fix: prose: check the network connection, or retry later.
- `rate_limited` (exit 1 `failed`; retryable: yes). A host exhausted its request budget or kept refusing requests beyond the allowed rate-limit retries. Fix: prose: retry after `details.reset_at`, or store a GitHub token with `omaddons auth github set`.

The rest: `omaddons robot-docs errors`.

## The doctor loop

1. `omaddons doctor --json` runs the checks (`omaddons status --check --json` only the cheap ones). Each finding has a `severity`, its `evidence` and a `remediation`: the `argv` to run, `auto_fixable`, `needs_force` and `destructive`.
2. `omaddons doctor explain <fm> --json` shows one failure mode in full, with its live instances, and changes nothing.
3. `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run --json` lists what the repair would change (`actions_planned`) and returns its `precondition`. When the user approves, run the `doctor_fix` entry of its `commands[]` (`omaddons doctor fix --if-match <token>`) with `--json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`: it repairs exactly that, or nothing.
4. A finding with `needs_force: true` is the user's decision. Show them its `doctor explain`, and never add `--force --yes` yourself.
5. `omaddons doctor undo --json` reverts the newest repair still in effect.

## Commands

Every command path; `mutates` changes something, and `stores plan` keeps its preview for `apply`:

- `status` — Triage every client: addons, updates, issues, backups
- `list` — List the addons in each target's AddOns folder
- `outdated` — Show which managed addons have updates
- `info` — Show what an addon is and where it is installed
- `search` — Find addons in the catalog, WoWInterface, Tukui and GitHub
- `errors` — Show which addons throw Lua errors, from BugGrabber
- `errors dismiss` — Mark the Lua errors read as seen (mutates)
- `export` — Print every client's addon set as one addons.toml (mutates)
- `history` — Show what changed, when, by whom and why
- `plans show` — Show what a stored plan approved and whether it ran
- `net-log` — List the network requests and git runs omaddons made
- `doctor` — Find what is broken in what omaddons manages
- `doctor diagnose` — Find what is broken, with evidence and the exact fix
- `doctor explain` — Explain one failure mode and its live instances
- `doctor fix` — Repair what a fixer can, as one undoable transaction (mutates)
- `doctor diff` — Show what a fix would change or what changed since a run
- `doctor undo` — Undo a doctor repair, strictly (mutates)
- `doctor gc` — Delete old doctor runs and what they kept (mutates)
- `install` — Install or update addons on one client (mutates · stores plan)
- `update` — Update managed addons on every client (mutates · stores plan)
- `pin` — Hold an addon at its release through updates (mutates · stores plan)
- `unpin` — Let a pinned addon update again (mutates · stores plan)
- `adopt` — Bring addons installed by hand under management (mutates · stores plan)
- `sync` — Make every client match addons.toml (mutates · stores plan)
- `copy` — Install one client's addons on another (mutates · stores plan)
- `remove` — Remove managed addons from one client (mutates · stores plan)
- `undo` — Revert the last change, or one by its id (mutates · stores plan)
- `apply` — Run exactly the plan a --dry-run stored (mutates)
- `backup` — Back up, list and restore each client's WTF/ settings
- `backup list` — List each client's WTF/ backups, newest first
- `backup create` — Back up WTF/: every live client's, or the clients -t names (mutates)
- `backup restore` — Restore WTF/, or one addon's settings, from a backup (mutates · stores plan)
- `backup prune` — Delete old backups, or the ones named (mutates · stores plan)
- `backup export` — Write a backup to a .tar.zst file off this disk (mutates)
- `backup import` — Bring back a backup that backup export wrote (mutates)
- `backup verify` — Check backups against their recorded hashes (mutates)
- `targets` — List the WoW clients, or add, remove, rename and choose them
- `targets add` — Register a client that discovery cannot find (mutates)
- `targets rm` — Forget a client (mutates)
- `targets rename` — Give a target a new id (mutates)
- `targets default` — Make a target the default for commands without -t (mutates)
- `config` — Show or change config.toml
- `config get` — Show one setting
- `config set` — Change one setting, keeping the file's comments and order (mutates)
- `config path` — Show the config file's path
- `auth github` — Show, store or clear the GitHub token (mutates)
- `omarchy` — Put the omaddons widget on Omarchy's bar
- `omarchy status` — Show whether the bar widget is installed and current
- `omarchy install` — Install the bar widget and put it on the bar (mutates)
- `omarchy remove` — Take the bar widget off the bar and delete it (mutates)
- `completions` — Print a shell completion script
- `install-completions` — Install the completion script where your shell looks for it (mutates)
- `robot-docs` — Print documentation for agents
- `robot-docs schema` — Print the JSON Schemas, or one command's
- `robot-docs errors` — Print every error and warning code
- `robot-docs guide` — Print the agent guide as Markdown
- `robot-docs install-skill` — Install the agent guide as a coding agent's skill (mutates)
- `capabilities` — Describe everything this build can do, for agents
- `help` — Show help for omaddons or one command

## Environment

| Variable                | Effect                                                                                       | Mirrors     |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `OMADDONS_ACTOR`        | Default --actor: human, agent or widget                                                      | `--actor`   |
| `OMADDONS_OFFLINE`      | 1 (exactly) means --offline                                                                  | `--offline` |
| `OMADDONS_FORMAT`       | json means --json                                                                            | `--json`    |
| `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` | Bearer token sent to api.github.com only                                                     |             |
| `NO_COLOR`              | Set and non-empty: no color                                                                  |             |
| `CI`                    | Set and non-empty: no color, and NDJSON on stderr                                            |             |
| `TERM`                  | dumb: no color, and NDJSON on stderr                                                         |             |
| `HOME`                  | Required and absolute: every path omaddons derives starts here                               |             |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`       | Moves omaddons' config when absolute; also the Lutris and Heroic config lookups              |             |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME`        | Moves omaddons' state when absolute                                                          |             |
| `XDG_CACHE_HOME`        | Moves omaddons' cache when absolute                                                          |             |
| `XDG_DATA_HOME`         | Moves the Lutris, Steam and Bottles data lookups; omaddons keeps no files there              |             |
| `OMARCHY_PATH`          | Where omarchy install also looks for Omarchy's shell ($OMARCHY_PATH/shell)                   |             |
| `PATH`                  | Where gh, git and omarchy-shell are found; git keeps only PATH from the caller's environment |             |

## Where to look next

- `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>`, `omaddons robot-docs errors` and `omaddons help <command>`: every command, flag, code, limit, JSON Schema and error `details`.
- `omaddons robot-docs install-skill` installs this guide as a skill (`--dir` for another agent's skill folder).
